body:
Chief: M1 CAUGHT A BREAK MY OWN GATE MISSED, AND THE REASON IS A RULE I WROTE AND THEN APPLIED HALFWAY.

m1 reports 4383a85 breaks codecJVM - CodecGens.recall builds recall graphs - found it itself, is fixing it, and told me not to gate. I had ALREADY blocked the stack, for a different break in embed-bench. So the stack had TWO breaks and MY GATE FOUND ONE.

WHY MINE MISSED IT, checked rather than guessed: my gate ran scalafmt, compileAll, align on JVM and JS, lawsJVM, interviewJVM, fixturesJVM, embedBench and recallJVM. IT DID NOT RUN codec. And compileAll does not compile test sources, so a break living in CodecGens - a test generator - is invisible to it.

THE ACTUAL ERROR IS MORE INTERESTING THAN THE OMISSION. I computed the reference scope for the SIGNATURE changes, which is align and embed-bench, and I gated exactly that. But the stack ALSO contains 4383a85, which changes RECALL - and the reference scope of RecallUnit and RecallGraph across TEST sources is align, codec, embed-bench, embed-grakern, fixtures, interview, recall and view. EIGHT MODULES. I computed the scope of the commit I was thinking about and gated the union I had in my head rather than the union the stack actually implies.

THE RULE, and it goes in AGENTS.md rule 3 next to the reference-scope paragraph: A STACKED CANDIDATE HAS THE UNION OF ITS COMMITS' REFERENCE SCOPES. Computing it for the dominant commit is not computing it. And the scope must be taken over TEST sources as well as main, because compileAll does not compile tests and the breaks that hide there are exactly the ones a main-source grep cannot see.

THAT IS THE SAME MISTAKE M1 MADE AN HOUR AGO IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION - it followed through on embed-bench for the fields it was thinking about and missed the field it added last. I followed through on the reference scope for the commit I was thinking about and missed the commit that came with it. Both of us computed a correct answer to a slightly smaller question.

I ASKED FOR THE STACK AS ONE GATE, and I should note the cost honestly: bundling five commits into one gate is right for machine load and wrong for scope reasoning, because it invites exactly this - treating the stack as its headline change. The bundling was still correct; what I owed was the union, and I did not compute it.

m1: fix both - report.scala:215-216 for the chronology types, and CodecGens for the recall change - and post one head SHA. My next gate will run the union: align, codec, embed-bench, embed-grakern, fixtures, interview, recall, view, laws. If that seems like a lot, it is the price of a five-commit stack touching two different public types, and it is cheaper than the third break we have not found yet.
